# HEART

**H**eterogeneity-aware **E**mpowerment via **A**daptive **R**obust
**T**ransfer for target-population inference.

HEART tests variant–trait associations in a small target population (for
example, an under-represented ancestry in a biobank) and borrows
strength from a larger source population. It does not assume that
genetic effects are shared between the two populations. Source-specific
signals do not inflate the error rate, and HEART is asymptotically no
less powerful than a target-only analysis.

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("haoyu-yang001/HEART", build_vignettes = TRUE)
```

Documentation: <https://haoyu-yang001.github.io/HEART/>

## Method in brief

For each variant *j*:

1.  **Estimation and decorrelation**
    ([`heart_assoc()`](https://haoyu-yang001.github.io/HEART/reference/heart_assoc.md)).
    HEART computes the target-only estimator β̂^(tar) and an auxiliary
    estimator β̂^(aux). The auxiliary estimator is pooled, doubly robust
    (DR, using surrogate-based synthetic outcomes), or source-only. It
    is then decorrelated from the target-only estimator using their
    joint sandwich covariance:

    β̂^(de) = β̂^(aux) − ρ̂ β̂^(tar), with ρ̂ = Ĉov(β̂^(aux), β̂^(tar)) /
    V̂ar(β̂^(tar)).

    This step gives asymptotically independent p-values (p_(tar),
    p_(de)).

2.  **Adaptive transfer via null decomposition**
    ([`heart_test()`](https://haoyu-yang001.github.io/HEART/reference/heart_test.md)).
    The target null H₀: β^(tar) = 0 is split into H₀₀ ∪ H₀₁. A
    four-group mixture model on (p_(tar), p_(de)) gives the HEART
    statistic

    T = π̂₀₀/(Ĉ₁Ĉ₂α̂₁α̂₂) · p_(tar)^(1−α̂₁) p_(de)^(1−α̂₂) + π̂₀₁/(Ĉ₁α̂₁) ·
    p_(tar)^(1−α̂₁).

    HEART estimates the composite null distribution of T from the data.
    This gives per-variant HEART p-values, FDR q-values and
    FWER-adjusted p-values.

## Quick start

``` r

library(HEART)
sim <- heart_simulate(n_tar = 2000, n_src = 20000, J = 2000, seed = 1)

res <- heart(Y = sim$Y, G = sim$G, D = sim$D, X = sim$X, aux = "pooled", alpha = 0.05)
res                       # summary of estimated parameters and discoveries
head(res$results)         # p_tar, p_de, log_T, p_heart, q_heart, padj_fwer, reject_*
```

## Genome-wide analysis in chunks

[`heart_test()`](https://haoyu-yang001.github.io/HEART/reference/heart_test.md)
must see **all** variants, because the four-group parameters are
estimated genome-wide. Step 1 can be split across jobs:

``` r

library(BEDMatrix)
G <- BEDMatrix("chr22.bed", simple_names = TRUE)        # rows must align with Y, D, X
idx <- match(sample_ids, rownames(G))

# --- one array job: a chunk of variants ---
fit_chunk <- heart_assoc(Y, G[idx, chunk_cols], D, X, aux = "pooled")
saveRDS(fit_chunk, sprintf("assoc_chunk%03d.rds", chunk_id))

# --- after all jobs finish ---
fit <- do.call(rbind, lapply(list.files(pattern = "^assoc_chunk"), readRDS))
res <- heart_test(fit$p_tar, fit$p_de_pooled, snp = fit$snp, alpha = 0.05)
```

For the Gaussian family the per-variant cost is linear in the number of
covariates. The computation uses the Frisch–Waugh–Lovell representation
of the sandwich (co)variances and is vectorised over blocks of variants.

## Doubly robust auxiliary estimator with surrogates

``` r

# 1. Train a prediction model for Y from surrogates S on a held-out split,
#    then predict Y_hat on the analysis sample (e.g. ranger::ranger).
# 2. Density ratio c_i = P(D = 1 | S) / P(D = 1):
c_i <- heart_density_ratio(D, W = S)
# 3. Use aux = "dr":
fit <- heart_assoc(Y, G, D, X, aux = "dr", Y_hat = Y_hat, c_i = c_i)
res <- heart_test(fit$p_tar, fit$p_de_dr)
```

## Summary statistics only

When the target and source studies are independent,
[`heart_meta()`](https://haoyu-yang001.github.io/HEART/reference/heart_meta.md)
builds the decorrelated inverse-variance meta-analytic estimator from
(β̂, SE) of each study:

``` r

m   <- heart_meta(beta_tar, se_tar, beta_src, se_src, snp = snp_ids)
res <- heart_test(m$p_tar, m$p_de_meta, snp = m$snp)
```

## Main functions

| Function | Purpose |
|----|----|
| [`heart()`](https://haoyu-yang001.github.io/HEART/reference/heart.md) | End-to-end analysis (Step 1 + Step 2) |
| [`heart_assoc()`](https://haoyu-yang001.github.io/HEART/reference/heart_assoc.md) | Target-only, auxiliary (`pooled` / `dr` / `source`) and decorrelated estimators; Gaussian or binomial |
| [`heart_density_ratio()`](https://haoyu-yang001.github.io/HEART/reference/heart_density_ratio.md) | Density ratio for the DR estimator |
| [`heart_meta()`](https://haoyu-yang001.github.io/HEART/reference/heart_meta.md) | Decorrelated meta-analysis from summary statistics |
| [`heart_test()`](https://haoyu-yang001.github.io/HEART/reference/heart_test.md) | HEART statistic, composite null distribution, FDR / FWER control |
| [`heart_pi_estimate()`](https://haoyu-yang001.github.io/HEART/reference/heart_pi_estimate.md), [`heart_tail_estimate()`](https://haoyu-yang001.github.io/HEART/reference/heart_tail_estimate.md) | Four-group proportions and tail parameters |
| [`heart_statistic()`](https://haoyu-yang001.github.io/HEART/reference/heart_statistic.md), [`heart_null_cdf()`](https://haoyu-yang001.github.io/HEART/reference/heart_null_cdf.md) | Statistic and null CDF (F₀₀, Q̂, F̂₀₁, N̂, F̂₀) |
| [`heart_simulate()`](https://haoyu-yang001.github.io/HEART/reference/heart_simulate.md) | Toy data under the four-group model |

## Citation

Yang H, Wang R, Lin X. *Heterogeneity-aware Empowerment via Adaptive
Robust Transfer for target-population inference.* (manuscript)

# Package index

## End-to-end analysis

- [`heart()`](https://haoyu-yang001.github.io/HEART/reference/heart.md)
  : HEART: end-to-end analysis from individual-level data

## Step 1: estimation and decorrelation

- [`heart_assoc()`](https://haoyu-yang001.github.io/HEART/reference/heart_assoc.md)
  : Per-variant target-only, auxiliary and decorrelated estimators
- [`heart_density_ratio()`](https://haoyu-yang001.github.io/HEART/reference/heart_density_ratio.md)
  : Density ratio between the target and the pooled population
- [`heart_meta()`](https://haoyu-yang001.github.io/HEART/reference/heart_meta.md)
  : Decorrelated inverse-variance meta-analysis from summary statistics

## Step 2: adaptive transfer via null decomposition

- [`heart_test()`](https://haoyu-yang001.github.io/HEART/reference/heart_test.md)
  : HEART test: adaptive transfer via null decomposition
- [`heart_pi_estimate()`](https://haoyu-yang001.github.io/HEART/reference/heart_pi_estimate.md)
  : Estimate the four-group proportions from a pair of p-value sequences
- [`heart_tail_estimate()`](https://haoyu-yang001.github.io/HEART/reference/heart_tail_estimate.md)
  : Estimate the left-tail parameters of the alternative p-value density
- [`heart_statistic()`](https://haoyu-yang001.github.io/HEART/reference/heart_statistic.md)
  : HEART test statistic
- [`heart_null_cdf()`](https://haoyu-yang001.github.io/HEART/reference/heart_null_cdf.md)
  : Composite null distribution of the HEART statistic

## Simulation

- [`heart_simulate()`](https://haoyu-yang001.github.io/HEART/reference/heart_simulate.md)
  : Simulate target / source data under the four-group model

- [`HEART`](https://haoyu-yang001.github.io/HEART/reference/HEART-package.md)
  [`HEART-package`](https://haoyu-yang001.github.io/HEART/reference/HEART-package.md)
